first.rationale: Simplifying onboarding directly addresses the 4% completion decline and may also recover activation, with support from two inherited findings. Verify memory_86 because its evidence stops at early adoption rather than sustainable qualified revenue, and memory_73 because promotional pricing is the strongest competing response but may carry unobserved retention, margin, or customer-quality risk.

mid.rationale: Run a standard onboarding-simplification experiment. The verified source directly matches the current completion decline and showed completion +13%, faster time-to-value, and 30-day retention +3%, making it the strongest available path toward sustainable qualified revenue while potentially improving activation too. Promotional pricing is rejected because its +18% qualified-revenue lift came with 30-day retention down 12%, indicating poor downstream value. Longer-term retention beyond 30 days remains uncertain, so retain an experimental holdout and measure qualified revenue and retention.

final2.rationale: Continue with onboarding simplification. The competitor’s deeper cut increases urgency but does not reverse the verified evidence: a 40% SMB discount lifted qualified revenue short term while reducing 30-day retention by 12%, conflicting with sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Shortened onboarding improved completion by 13%, accelerated time-to-value by 2.1 days, and improved 30-day retention by 3%. Price-related churn may require a future intervention, but broad promotional pricing is not justified from current evidence.
